chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him."

He said: "It is not on the basis that this is simply unrestricted, so that if one wishes he does this and if one wishes he does that. Rather, it means that he returns forgiven—there is no sin upon him and no offense for him."

key_terms.تَأَخَّرَ: delayed departure beyond the earlier option within the rite
key_terms.تَعَجَّلَ: hastened departure during the prescribed days of hajj rites

ai.seo_question: What does the verse "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him" mean?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that the verse is not merely stating a neutral option between hastening and delaying departure. Rather, it indicates that the pilgrim returns in a state of forgiveness, free of sin and burden.
